subject: Eventstream sweep & privacy clearance - request
messages:
From: James Smith <j.smith@acme-payments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-payments.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Observed anomalous event — please advise

Hi Ben,

We saw an alert early this morning tied to an internal event stream (event id: evt-9f3a). The alert shows a spike in outbound requests from a processing shard that normally has very low activity. Attached is the alert screenshot and a short timeline from our SRE tool.

Our legal/compliance team is asking us to confirm whether any customer-identifiable records may have left Redwood systems or whether there was any unauthorized access to customer payloads. Can you confirm what Redwood can see on your side and whether you can quickly validate that no PII/customer records were exfiltrated?

Time window to review: 2026-12-12 02:00:00 - 2026-12-12 03:30:00 UTC (approx).

We appreciate a quick initial read — if it helps we can jump on a short call.

Thanks,
James
James Smith
Head of Security Operations
Acme Payments

Attachment: alert-screenshot.png (image/png, 142 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: James Smith <j.smith@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observed anomalous event — please advise

Hi James — thanks for the heads up and for the screenshot. I'm Ben on the incidents team; we've kicked off a focused triage for the time window you cited. Initial steps we've taken: 

- Isolated the affected shard from the routing pool to prevent further requests.
- Captured live eventstream snapshots and rotated the KV cache read handle for integrity checks.
- Spun up a hash-verify job against the archived request/response blobs for the 02:00–03:30 UTC window.

We're pulling logs and running checksum comparisons against backed-up traces; I'll share initial indicators ASAP. Stephanie is leading the log sweep and will post a detailed readout this afternoon.

If you have any additional trace ids or example request IDs from your alert, please drop them here.

Ben Carter
Incidents Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: initial-triage-checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 34 KB)

Subject: Re: Observed anomalous event — please advise — eventstream sweep results

Hi James / Ben,

Summary of findings from the eventstream sweep and integrity checks:

- Scope: evaluated all requests and internal routing telemetry for the shard and timeframe 2026-12-12 02:00:00 — 2026-12-12 03:30:00 UTC.
- Data sources examined: live eventstream snapshots, archived trace blobs (cold storage), routing logs, KV-cache access logs, outbound flow logs.
- Method: checksum + signature validation (SHA-256) against archived blobs; cross-checked request payload hashes against retention backups; compared outbound destinations to allowlist.

Key results:
- No successful authentication bypass or credential misuse detected.
- No request payloads matching customer-identifiable record patterns were transmitted to external destinations.
- Hash reconciliation completed for 100% of trace blobs in the time window — no mismatches found.
- A small number of transient retries triggered alerting noise (flaky endpoint), but those requests were internal retries and did not contain persisted customer payloads.

Attachments: sweep-report-20261212.csv (contains redacted trace ids and checksums). We retained raw artifact bundles for Acme legal review; see Drive link below.

Recommended next steps:
1) Redwood can provide a signed short-form statement for your records (see Ben's follow-up planned).
2) If you'd like a joint session with Acme SRE + Redwood incidents team, we can do a technical walkthrough of the sweep and artifacts.

Please let us know if you'd like additional evidence or a specific redaction format for the report.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Reliability Engineer, Incidents
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
